messages:
alex: Quick sync — thinking about the SDK surface for paginated streaming: adaptive retry window (dynamically expand retry window for resuming) vs simple prefetch+retry. Need to decide default behavior across Python/TS/Go.

maria: Short take: adaptive window saves tokens on average but is trickier to reason about across transports. Prefetch is predictable but can double-count tokens when you abort.

simon: For Go users (server-side) explicit control is preferred. I'd rather expose prefetch_size + a simple retry_backoff config than a black-box adaptive thing.

riyad: We also need to consider transport capability: gRPC/stream can resume with continuation tokens; REST long-poll/streaming is less forgiving — resume often requires server-side support. That impacts whether adaptive window is feasible.

alex: Good point. Thinking about 3 concerns: latency (client-perceived), cost (extra tokens), and complexity (surface ergonomic + cross-lang).

maria: Could we have a unified surface but different defaults per SDK? e.g. TS default=low-prefetch for webapps, Go default=explicit prefetch=5, Py default=adaptive-opt-in?

alex: That might work. Suggest surface: { mode: "prefetch" | "adaptive" | "none", prefetch_size: number, retry_window_ms: number, max_resume_attempts: number }

simon: API suggestion looks fine. For Go, keep types explicit: PagerConfig{Mode, Prefetch, RetryWindow, MaxAttempts}. Avoid hidden heuristics.

riyad: Implementation note: adaptive requires tracking sequence gaps and a KV cache of last N tokens + server-side support to apply a resume offset. If server can't replay token stream we fall back to prefetch. Need a clear fallback policy.

alex: Do we want SDKs to automatically downgrade to prefetch when transport lacks resume? I vote yes, but with an opt-out flag so platform teams can opt for strict behavior.

maria: Agreed. Also add telemetry hooks: emit events when fallback happens and when a resume succeeds/fails. That will help Optimize recommendations.

alex: Example TS config:```ts
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  pager: {
    mode: 'adaptive', // fallback to prefetch if transport can't resume
    prefetch_size: 2,
    retry_window_ms: 250,
    max_resume_attempts: 3
  }
});
```

simon: One more tradeoff: prefetch_size=1 gives lowest extra tokens but highest request count. For high QPS workloads we should recommend batching at transport layer.

maria: Ops concern: for Dedicated/private customers we should expose server-side toggles so they can enable resume-support; otherwise adaptive mode should be disabled by default.

alex: Next steps: I'll draft a short RFC with the proposed surface, per-SDK default table, and perf estimates (latency vs token cost). If no objections by EOD, I'll open impl PRs. @maria @simon @riyad please flag anything missing. :thumbsup:
